overview: The Medford Energy and Environment Committee welcomed new members, reviewed recent Massachusetts climate legislation, and discussed city sustainability projects. Members also brainstormed priority advocacy initiatives for 2025 and set plans for upcoming meetings and community events.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the previous meeting's minutes following a brief update on grocery store plastic film recycling.

items.title: Member Introductions
items.summary: Committee members and new appointees introduced themselves and shared their professional backgrounds and environmental interests.

items.title: Administrative Updates and Upcoming Schedule
items.summary: Staff announced a job vacancy for an economic development planner and confirmed climate scientist Matt Barlow will present at the February meeting.

items.title: Presentation on Massachusetts Climate Legislation
items.summary: Bob Paine summarized provisions of newly enacted Massachusetts climate legislation, prompting discussion on energy siting reforms, EV charging infrastructure, nuclear energy, and networked geothermal utilities.

items.title: City Climate Planner Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike reported on Electrify Medford coaching numbers, acceptance into the Mass Save Community First Partnership, Andrews and McGlynn school HVAC and solar projects, and pending state decarbonization proposals.

items.title: 2025 Action Initiatives and Committee Priorities
items.summary: Members brainstormed focus areas for the upcoming year, including amending the plastic bag ordinance, consumer warnings regarding third-party energy scams, rooftop solar policy, rodenticide restrictions, and zero-waste programming.

items.title: New Business
items.summary: The committee discussed preliminary scheduling for the annual Harvest Your Energy Festival and potential guest presentations from local zero-waste organizations.
